title: October 16, 2014: India launched the third satellite of a navigation system it was building entirely on its own.

sources.text: President of India - press release congratulating ISRO on the successful launch of PSLV-C26
Deccan Herald - ISRO successfully launches IRNSS-1C

caption:
October 16, 2014: India launched the third satellite of a navigation system it was building entirely on its own.

The 1,425 kg satellite was the third of seven planned for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System - what would later be called NavIC - reaching its intended orbit about 20 minutes after liftoff.

The President of India issued a formal note of congratulations, calling it a step toward India having its own satellite-based navigation system - independent of the GPS systems built and controlled by other countries.

Building a satellite constellation one launch at a time, rather than relying on a foreign system, gave India a navigation capability under its own control - for its military, its ships and eventually its phones.
